title: Who Does What: Operations & My Care
subtitle: Operations & My Care
notes: Companion: Dr. Omar char-omar-welcome, L1 half-body bottom-right (alt: Dr. Omar, the course guide, welcoming the learner). Speaker: Omar. Brand kit draft in use ⚠ Draft — pending D11.
narration_text: Dr. Omar: Welcome to Who Does What: Operations & My Care. You will practise decisions that help you act with confidence. You will leave with practical actions for your next shift.

title: Why it matters
body_html:
“Right team, first time.”

A patient shouldn't have to tell their story twice.
notes: Companion: Dr. Omar char-omar-explaining, L3 right column (media of the text_media layout). Speaker: Omar. Omar's three-desks story is used here once (companions.md §1).
narration_text: Dr. Omar: Routing matters. A patient who repeats their story loses trust. I once sent the same patient to three desks in one morning. She never forgot it — and neither did I. Keep the main point connected to a familiar task or conversation. That connection makes the information easier to use when it matters. Use the principle in context.

title: Patient journey
image_alt: Patient journey from booking to follow-up: six numbered stages in a row — Book, Arrive, Consult, Services and pharmacy, Leave, Follow-up.
prompt_html:
Open all 6 stages. Each stage shows which team leads: Operations, My Care or both.

Stage leads ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

regions.feedback_html: Registration and priority bookings sit with My Care. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
The on-site team welcomes the patient and runs the front of house: look and feel, and on-spot inquiries. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
Operations supports doctors and nurses so the consultation runs on time. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
Operations tracks the Lab, Radiology and Pharmacy KPIs, including turnaround time (TAT). ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
Operations closes the visit; My Care picks up post-consultation follow-ups, referrals and disposition. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
Post-consultation and monthly follow-ups, insurance and medication follow-ups and programme coordination are My Care work. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

feedback.correct_html: You have opened all six stages. Operations runs the visit; My Care carries the relationship before and after it.
feedback.incorrect_html: Open each of the six stage markers to see which team leads.

notes: Hotspot circles use the ops-img-journey.svg pixel space (1600 × 900): stage circles cx 220/450/680/910/1140/1370, cy 450, r 72. Stage-lead assignments derived from the slide 2/5 activity lists ⚠ Draft — pending B7. No companion.
narration_text: Dr. Omar: Walk the journey. Notice where each team leads. Let each marker add context rather than rushing to a conclusion. The full picture matters before a workplace decision is made. Keep the next action clear. Think of the first detail you would check. Apply the point to a familiar task.

narration_text: Dr. Omar: Operations runs the day: environment, KPIs, recovery on the spot. Use each section to build the picture step by step. Before moving on, identify the action or check that belongs to your role. Ask early when a situation does not match the rule. Good habits here are quiet: check, confirm, continue. Pause and connect this to your role. Use the principle in context. Keep the next action clear. Think of the first detail you would check. Apply the point to a familiar task. Carry the idea into your next decision.

title: Sort the work
prompt_html: Place each of the 10 activities with the team that owns it: Operations or My Care.

items.text_html: On-spot complaint at reception ⚠ Draft — pending B7

targets.label_html: My Care — the relationship after the visit

feedback.correct_html:
Correct. Operations owns what happens in the clinic today: KPIs such as lab TAT, look and feel, the end-to-end journey, support for doctors and on-spot complaints. My Care owns the ongoing relationship: follow-up calls, insurance and medication follow-ups, programme bookings, telemedicine coordination and referral priority.

Overlap: both teams handle inquiries and complaints. A complaint made in the clinic right now goes to Operations; a service issue after the visit goes to My Care. Routing rule ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
feedback.incorrect_html: Not all 10 yet. Ask: is this happening in the clinic during today's visit (Operations), or is it part of the patient's care before or after the visit (My Care)? Inquiries and complaints sit in both lists — where and when the patient raises it decides the owner. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

notes: Card answers follow the Phase 0 verified-facts lists (slides 2 and 5). The card asks for feedback on each card; edumints drag_drop has no per-item feedback, so the overlap explanation is in the screen feedback. Overlap items ⚠ Draft — pending B7. Keyboard pick-and-place is the player's default. No companion.

title: Who do I call?
intro_html:
Four patient requests. Route each one to the right team and role, first time. Pass with 3 of 4.

Routing answers ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

nodes.image_alt: A patient talks to a patient-experience officer at a clinic reception desk.
nodes.prompt_html: Request 1 of 4. At reception, a patient is upset: her lab result promised for today isn't ready. Who handles it?

choices.feedback_html: Yes. On-the-spot complaints and service recovery are Operations' job, led by the PX team on site. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
My Care follows patients up after the visit. A complaint in the clinic right now needs the on-site PX team (Operations). ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

choices.text_html: Tell her to call back tomorrow
choices.feedback_html: Sending her away means she tells her story twice. The PX officer on site (Operations) owns recovery now. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

nodes.image_alt: A My Care coordinator on a phone follow-up call with a patient.
nodes.prompt_html: Request 2 of 4. A diabetic patient asks who will remind him about his 3-month review.

choices.text_html: My Care — his coordinator handles follow-ups and bookings
choices.feedback_html: Right. Follow-ups and programme bookings are My Care work; the My Care Coordinator keeps the review on track. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

choices.text_html: Operations — the PX officer at reception
choices.feedback_html: The PX officer looks after today's visit. A review in three months is part of the ongoing relationship: My Care. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

choices.text_html: He should set his own reminder
choices.feedback_html: Follow-up reminders are a My Care service. Route him to his My Care Coordinator. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

nodes.image_alt: A staff member on an insurance call about a patient's medication approval.
nodes.prompt_html: Request 3 of 4. A patient's insurer rejected his monthly medication.

choices.text_html: My Care — insurance and medication follow-up
choices.feedback_html: Correct. Insurance and medication follow-ups are listed under My Care. The coordinator follows the rejection through. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
Operations runs the clinic day. Insurance and medication follow-ups belong to My Care. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
The pharmacy dispenses, but following up an insurance rejection for monthly medication is a My Care task. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

nodes.image_alt: Patients waiting in a pharmacy queue in a clinic.
nodes.prompt_html: Request 4 of 4. A doctor reports the pharmacy queue is causing delays every afternoon.

choices.text_html: Operations — pharmacy KPIs and daily operations
choices.feedback_html: Yes. Pharmacy KPIs, the patient journey and support for doctors are Operations' job. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
The My Care QA leader checks the quality of My Care calls and service. A queue in the clinic is daily operations: Operations. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
Operations supports doctors and nurses so they can focus on care. Report the queue to Operations. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.

feedback.correct_html: Well routed. In-clinic issues today go to Operations; follow-ups, programmes and insurance go to My Care. ⚠ Draft — pending B7.
feedback.incorrect_html: Review each request: is it happening in the clinic now (Operations), or part of the patient's ongoing care (My Care)? Try again.

title: Escalation
prompt_html:
The PX officer can't resolve a complaint on the spot. Who is the next step?

Escalation line ⚠ Draft — pending B1.

options.feedback_html: Correct. On the draft Operations chart, PXOs report to the PX Managers at their site, so the site PX Manager is the next step. ⚠ Draft — pending B1.
The Director leads the whole structure. Escalate one step at a time: the PXO's own line manager comes first.
Coordinators handle follow-ups and bookings in My Care. An on-site complaint stays in the Operations line.
The QA leader checks the quality of My Care calls and service, not on-site complaint escalation.

feedback.correct_html: Correct. The next step is the site Patient Experience Manager — one level up the Operations line. ⚠ Draft — pending B1.
feedback.incorrect_html: Look again at the Operations structure: who sits directly above the PXOs at a site?

notes: Correct answer from the card (site Patient Experience Manager, per B1) ⚠ Draft — pending B1. Distractors are roles shown on ops-011/ops-021. No companion over the question.

title: Roles
prompt_html: Match each role with what it does.

pairs.right_html: Quality of My Care calls and service

feedback.correct_html: Correct. Knowing what each role does tells you who to call: the PXO for the visit today, the coordinator for follow-ups, the onboarding leader for enrolment, the Operations Sr. Manager for the clinic day and the QA leader for My Care service quality.
feedback.incorrect_html: Not all five. Think about where each role works: on site during the visit (Operations) or with the patient over time (My Care).

notes: Pairs verbatim from the card. Role titles follow the draft charts ⚠ Draft — pending B1 / B2. No companion.

title: Close
body_html:
Right team, first time

  • Operations runs the visit: environment, KPIs, recovery on the spot.
  • My Care carries the relationship: follow-ups, programmes, insurance, referrals.
  • Route by where and when: in the clinic now, or the patient's ongoing care.
  • Escalate one step at a time, by role.

Names: use the live staff directory (intranet). Link ⚠ Draft — pending B6 / D5.

Next: module 05/06 (clinicians) or 08 (EHR).
notes: Companions: Dr. Omar char-omar-success + Noor char-noor-avatar-happy, L6. Two-voice close: omar-1 then noor-1, joined into one file. Staff-directory URL not yet supplied ⚠ Draft — pending B6 / D5.
narration_text: Dr. Omar: You can now use these key actions in your role. Keep the practical rule close, ask when you are unsure, and carry the next step into your shift. Take one clear next action with you. Noor: Carry this practical rule into your next decision.
